summary.title: RynnBrain 1.1: Towards More Capable and Generalizable Embodied Foundation Model

details: Embodied VLMs understand images/video well but their representations and outputs are not directly usable by robot manipulation policies, and it is unclear how well such a model serves as initialization for VLA post-training.

RynnBrain 1.1: a family of embodied foundation models (2B, 9B, 122B-A10B, built on Qwen3.5) trained with one unified spatio-temporal + physically-grounded autoregressive recipe in which language and spatial outputs (boxes, points, trajectories) share a single discretized token vocabulary.

Two new pretraining tasks that bring outputs closer to manipulation: (i) contact-point prediction, replacing grasp rectangles with a compact contact-centered target (grasp center point plus in-plane gripper angle), and (ii) native 3D grounding, predicting metric 9-DoF camera-frame 3D boxes (center, size, orientation) as discretized tokens from a single image plus intrinsics.

RynnBrain-VLA: flow-matching action-chunk policy on the same backbone with a shared 81-dimensional action space partitioned into semantically aligned body-part groups (arms, gripper, hand, torso, head) plus embodiment-specific masks, so heterogeneous robots train jointly in one policy without aligning incompatible low-level action spaces.

Decoder-only VLM with DeepStack and Interleaved MRoPE; scales 2B, 9B, 122B-A10B (MoE) initialized from Qwen3.5; identical infrastructure across scales (sequence-length-aware load balancing, per-sample loss reduction, ZeRO, expert parallelism).
AdamW, LR 5e-6 (2B) / 2e-6 (9B, 122B), global batch 512/1024/1024, warmup ratio 0.03; single causal LM loss over mixed text and spatial tokens.
Native 3D grounding added only to the 2B and 9B pretraining mixtures.

Capability-organized mixture: general MLLM (LLaVA-OV/Video, VL3, RynnBrain-Thinking), cognition (SenseNova-SI, VSI-590K, egocentric QA such as EgoTaskQA/RoboVQA), localization (RefSpatial, RoboAfford, MolmoAct trajectories), planning (AgibotWorld, Open X-Embodiment, Galaxea-G0 with Gemini-generated global instructions).

3D corpus: WildDet3D Essential (103K images / 374K verified boxes, 12K categories) + Synthetic (896K images) with Qwen-VL-generated referring queries, plus FoundationPose synthetic (1,849K images, noise-free boxes) as a metric-scale regularizer.

Contact points: 2.6M samples from Grasp-Anything, Jacquard V2, GraspFactory, GraspNet-1B, GraspClutter6D, produced by a view-conditioned rendering/projection pipeline with observability filtering; target serialized as (x,y) plus angle in [0,1000] normalized coords.

Backbone acts as a single-stream DiT; inputs packed as instruction + multi-camera observations + state + noisy action chunk; 32-step chunks with Real-Time Chunking (re-inference every 5 steps, guidance strength beta=10).

Three-layer deployment stack (model / 30 Hz + 200 Hz control loops / embodiment dispatch) on Unitree G1 (14D hand + separate 64D SONIC latent token, SONIC whole-body controller), Tianji-Wuji (54 active dims), Astribot S1 (23 active dims).

Controlled comparison: identical data, recipe and optimization (60k steps, LR 2e-5, batch 32, short side 384) for RynnBrain-VLA vs Qwen-Based-VLA; single-task policies vs one jointly trained generalist.

Base-model benchmarks: VSI-Bench, MMSI, ERQA, RoboSpatial (VQA/pointing), MindCube, EmbSpatial, RefSpatial-Bench and in-house RynnBrain-Object/Spatial/Grounding/Area/Affordance/Trajectory; 3D grounding on SUN RGB-D (AP@15) and WildDet3D-Bench (AP3D).

Baselines by scale: RynnBrain 1.0, Cosmos 3 / Cosmos-Reason2, SenseNova-SI, RoboBrain 2.0/2.5, Molmo2-ER, Pelican-VL, MiMo-Embodied, Qwen3.5 at matched size, plus Gemini 3 Pro, GPT 5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini Robotics-ER 1.5, HY-Embodied 0.5.

Real robot: three long-horizon multi-stage tasks (Sprinkle the Petals, Pour the Wine on Astribot; Grab the Spatulas on Tianji-Wuji), 20 trials each with randomized placements, reporting sub-task process score and full-task success; baselines GR00T N1.7 (chunk 40), pi0.5 (chunk 50), Qwen-Based-VLA.

key_findings.finding: Embodied capabilities scale non-uniformly, and reasoning-intensive spatial cognition scales positively only with embodied pretraining while the base VLM scales negatively.
key_findings.evidence: Across 2B to 122B-A10B under a unified recipe, RynnBrain 1.1 gains +38.6% on reasoning-intensive cognition while matched Qwen3.5 loses 39.2%, widening the gap from 18.2 to 50.8 points; on embodied localization the largest Qwen3.5 still trails the 2B RynnBrain, whereas general embodied cognition improves for both with a narrowing gap.

key_findings.finding: Initializing a VLA from the embodied base model, rather than the general VLM, substantially improves real-robot long-horizon manipulation and beats representative generalist VLAs.
key_findings.evidence: Under an identical post-training recipe, RynnBrain-VLA reaches 91.28% average process score / 86.67% success vs 68.33% / 60.00% for Qwen-Based-VLA (95% vs 50% on Grab the Spatulas), and exceeds GR00T N1.7 (83.31/73.33) and pi0.5 (72.44/65.00); on Unitree G1 Pull the Chair it achieves 90% vs 75% for GR00T N1.7 with the same SONIC controller.

key_findings.finding: Joint multi-task, multi-embodiment training in the masked unified action space yields positive transfer rather than interference relative to per-task policies.
key_findings.evidence: RynnBrain-VLA_Generalist improves average process score from 91.28% to 94.14% and success from 86.67% to 91.67%, with the largest gain on Pour the Wine (80% to 95% success).

key_findings.finding: The 122B-A10B model leads all evaluated proprietary and open-source models on several spatial reasoning and grounding benchmarks.
key_findings.evidence: Scores of 75.0 on VSI-Bench, 52.0 on MMSI, 79.1 on RefSpatial-Bench, 89.6 on MindCube and 86.6 on RynnBrain-Grounding, ahead of Gemini 3 Pro, GPT 5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini Robotics-ER 1.5, HY-Embodied 0.5 and Qwen3.5-122B-A10B; gains over RynnBrain 1.0 at 9B appear on eight of ten shared benchmarks (e.g. MindCube 56.6 to 86.9), though some 2B results (RoboSpatial, EmbSpatial) regress.

key_findings.finding: Adding explicit 3D supervision gives compact models competitive native language-conditioned metric 3D grounding that further benefits from scale.
key_findings.evidence: On SUN RGB-D, 2B reaches 34.28 AP@15 (above Seed1.5-VL 33.5 and Gemini 2.0 Pro 32.5) and 9B reaches 41.12 (Gemini Robotics-ER 48.3); on WildDet3D-Bench 2B gets 17.36 AP3D and 9B gets 23.44, surpassing the specialized WildDet3D detector at 22.6.
